About this opportunity
This role works directly for Ethos and is based in our London HQ, in Kings Cross. Successful candidates will be required to work in the office Monday to Thursday with Friday working remote.
Ethos is on a mission to make human opportunity abundant with AI. We use cutting-edge AI to match experts to paid opportunities at scale, from AI model training, investment research to full-time roles. We now pay out more than $1M/day to experts globally. Backed by world-leading investors including a16z, General Catalyst, XTX and more.
We're looking for a Compliance Associate to keep our platform, experts and clients safe as we grow. You'll be our first dedicated compliance hire, building our compliance foundations from the ground up. You'll own three connected areas: financial crime (KYC, AML and fraud) and regulation, data privacy, and information security. This is a hands-on role in a hyper-growth start-up. You'll review flagged cases, investigate suspicious activity and respond to data requests. You'll also write and own the policies behind that work. We're moving fast and you won't wait for problems to land; you'll go looking for them.
What you'll do
Financial crime and regulation
Build and own our KYC, AML, sanctions and fraud policies, including clear rules for edge cases. Put them into practice day to day, and update them as regulation changes
Own our identity verification setup, making verification smooth for genuine experts and hard for everyone else
Investigate suspicious activity, from fraud patterns and account takeovers to unusual payment or login behaviour, and work with engineering to turn what you find into automated checks
Handle KYC/KYB requests and compliance reporting for our banks, payment partners and clients, and escalate suspicious activity to the right people
Apply expert tax and payout rules, including W-8/W-9 forms, platform reporting rules (such as DAC7) and country-specific requirements
Data privacy
Handle data subject requests, such as access and erasure, within legal timeframes
Lead data protection impact assessments, and keep our privacy notices, records and retention rules current as the product evolves
Across Ethos
Keep a single compliance register of risks, controls and owners, and report monthly risk metrics to leadership and the board
Work with product, engineering and support to tighten controls without adding friction for experts
Who you are
2-5 years' experience in compliance, fraud or financial crime, ideally at a marketplace, or high volume payments startup
A strong grounding in KYC, AML, fraud and sanctions, and the judgement to apply them in proportion to the risk at a fast-moving business that isn’t a bank
Hands-on experience with an identity verification vendor such as Persona, Onfido, Sumsub or Veriff
Knowledge of UK GDPR and data protection is a big plus, or you're keen to learn it
A natural investigator: you read signals in context, not in isolation (a VPN flag on its own isn’t evidence of fraud), you know when to decide and when to escalate, and you handle sensitive information with discretion
Comfortable pulling and checking your own data with SQL or a BI tool, quick to learn new tools, and you never present numbers you haven’t verified
A clear writer who can explain a decision to an expert, a bank or the board
Proactive, independent, and at home with pace and ambiguity
Comfortable with pace and ambiguity in a fast-moving tech startup, with solid fundamentals and open to new ways of working
ICA or ACAMS certification is a plus
Why join Ethos
Work at the centre of the AI industry, on projects that shape how the next generation of AI is built
Be part of an ambitious team building something genuinely new, leveraging AI for the future of expertise
We've grown revenue 84x since our Series A in March 2026, and we're only just getting started!
Real ownership from the start. You'll run your own workstreams, not shadow someone else's
Key requirements
2-5 years' experience in compliance, fraud or financial crime, ideally at a marketplace, or high volume payments startup
A good amount of experience in KYC, AML, fraud and sanctions, and the judgement to apply them in proportion to the risk at a fast-moving business that isn’t a bank
Hands-on experience with an identity verification vendor such as Persona, Onfido, Sumsub or Veriff
Willingness to learn UK GDPR and data protection, gained experience is not essential
Familiarity with information security frameworks such as SOC 2 or ISO 27001, or the appetite to build it quickly
A natural investigator: you read signals in context, not in isolation (a VPN flag on its own isn’t evidence of fraud), you know when to decide and when to escalate, and you handle sensitive information with discretion
Comfortable pulling and checking your own data with SQL or a BI tool, quick to learn new tools, and you never present numbers you haven’t verified
A clear writer who can explain a decision to an expert, a bank or the board
Proactive, independent, and at home with pace and ambiguity
